text:
Alejandro R.: Quick Q — I'm planning to move my primary residence to Ciudad Juárez but will commute to the El Paso office ~3 days/week. Do I need to change my homebase? How will the WFH stipend be prorated if I'm ~60% in-office? Also wondering about customs/tax on shipping my company laptop to MX and any payroll withholding implications.

Maria (People Ops): Thanks for the heads up! Short answer: we need the Location Change form to start (link below). Homebase determines stipend currency/withholding and payroll reporting. If you keep US homebase vs switch to MX the impacts differ. Please submit the form and we'll loop payroll + legal.
<https://redwoodintra/people-ops/location-change>

Jake (Payroll): Flagging payroll — if homebase becomes Mexico, stipends convert to MXN and may be subject to Mexican social/withholding/reporting. If homebase stays US but you work physically in MX often, we still need to log days in MX for tax nexus reporting. Also, shipping laptops to MX can trigger import/customs paperwork and could be a taxable benefit depending on value.

Lauren (Legal): FYI legal perspective: cross-border daily commuting can raise payroll/reporting issues. Mexico has different rules around source-of-income and employer reporting; the 183-day rule is relevant for tax residency but not the only factor for payroll obligations. We'll need dates, residency intent, and expected split of days.

Alejandro R.: Timeline — plan to start local move 2024-05-15, expect ~4 nights/week in Juárez initially. Not planning >183 consecutive days abroad but it will be majority-of-days in MX some months. Anything urgent I should do to avoid gaps?

Maria (People Ops): Please submit the Location Change form today and mark the proposed start date. We'll mark this as "cross-border commuter" case and run the checklist. Stipend proration: if homebase MX, stipend pays MXN monthly; if US homebase retained, stipend stays USD but may be adjusted for local days. We'll confirm numbers after payroll review.

Finance Bot: Automated: Created ticket TICKET-4873 for cross-border location review. Expected turnaround: 5 business days.

Jake (Payroll): Alejandro — once form's in, send your passport + new address in a DM to payroll. We'll add a payroll flag and estimate the stipend proration. Typical approach: prorate by % of days declared remote vs in-office in a pay period.

Alejandro R.: Got it, uploading form now. Quick ask: is there any chance to request a temporary exception to keep US homebase for payroll continuity while I'm ramping the move?

Lauren (Legal): We can evaluate an exception for a transitional period. We'll need documentation of physical attendance at the US office (badging, calendar presence) and the exact dates. Legal + payroll will approve or propose mitigations.

Maria (People Ops): Great — once form is in we'll set a 15-min sync with payroll/legal if anything unclear. Thanks for flagging early! :calendar:

Alejandro R.: Thanks everyone — will post the form link + DM passport shortly.
